Summaries of decimal vectors

Source: R/decimal.R
decimal-summaries.Rd

sum(), prod(), mean(), min(), max() and range() compute in decimal arithmetic and return a decimal vector. Integer vectors can be mixed in; doubles and strings are refused, as they are in arithmetic.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'decimal'
mean(x, trim = 0, na.rm = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'decimal'
Summary(..., na.rm = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'decimal'
range(x, ..., na.rm = FALSE, finite = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'decimal'
min(x, ..., na.rm = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'decimal'
max(x, ..., na.rm = FALSE)

Arguments

x, ...

decimal or integer vectors. A decimal must come first; see "Put a decimal first".

trim

The fraction of values to drop from each end before averaging.

na.rm

Whether to remove missing values and NaNs first.

finite

Not supported; TRUE is an error.

Value

A decimal vector: of length two for range(), otherwise of length one.

Details

A missing value gives NA unless na.rm = TRUE. A NaN gives NaN, and a signaling NaN raises invalid_operation. na.rm = TRUE removes both missing values and NaNs, because is.na() is true for a NaN.

mean() sums the values, then divides under the active context. A trim between 0 and 0.5 drops floor(n * trim) values from each end of the sorted vector before averaging, and a trim of 0.5 or more gives the median, as in mean.default().

Put a decimal first

R picks the method for sum(), prod(), min(), max() and range() from the first argument alone. When that argument is not a decimal, R never calls these methods and treats a decimal as the text it stores. The package has no way to intercept this, nor to make it an error. In each case, put a decimal first or convert the first argument with as_decimal():

  • min(10L, x) compares text, so min(10L, decimal("9")) is "10". Write min(x, 10L) or min(as_decimal(10L), x).

  • max(2L, x) and range(2L, x) return a character vector. Write max(x, 2L) or range(as_decimal(2L), x).

  • sum(1L, x) and prod(1L, x) fail with "invalid 'type' (character) of argument". Write sum(x, 1L) or prod(as_decimal(1L), x).

  • pmax(2L, x) and pmin(2L, x) return a character vector. Write pmax(x, 2L) or pmax(as_decimal(2L), x).

pmax() and pmin() are not generic. With a decimal first they compare values, and stop with an error when a later argument has a finer scale than the first, because base R would give the result the first argument's scale: pmax(decimal("10"), decimal("9.5")) fails, while pmax(as_decimal(decimal("10"), scale = 1), decimal("9.5")) and pmax(decimal("9.5"), decimal("10")) work.

any() and all() are not supported for decimal vectors.

Examples

x <- decimal(c("9.50", "10", "2.25"))
sum(x)
#> <decimal[1]>
#> [1] 21.75
max(x, 12L)
#> <decimal[1]>
#> [1] 12.00
range(x)
#> <decimal[2]>
#> [1] 2.25  10.00
mean(decimal(c("1", "2", "3", "100")), trim = 0.25)
#> <decimal[1]>
#> [1] 2.5
